newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico retail sales fall in Q1, wholesale sales up.
newsitem.headline: Mexico retail sales fall in Q1, wholesale sales up.

text.p: Retail sales in Mexico during the first quarter fell by 3.5 percent compared to the same period the year before, while wholesale sales rose 1.2 percent, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) said on Wednesday.

INEGI gave no figures for March alone, but according to a Reuters calculation from INEGI data, the decline in retail sales during March was 3.8 percent from the same year-ago month. That figure was significantly worse than a Reuters survey which had forecast a retail sales decline in March of 0.69 percent.
In indexed data provided by INEGI, retail sales fell from 73.9 in March 1996 to 71.1 in March 1997. It said wholesale sales rose from 81.9 in March 1996 to 82.8 in March 1997.
Retail sales grew in real terms in the following areas:
furniture, domestic gas, cars, and supermarket and department stores. Retail sales fell in the areas of mom-and-pop stores, bookstores, records, toys, and clothing and footwear, INEGI said.
